name: When should I replace rather than restore smoke-damaged furniture?

mainEntity.name: When should I replace rather than restore smoke-damaged furniture?

acceptedAnswer.text: The decision to replace versus restore smoke-damaged furniture depends on the extent of the damage, the item's sentimental or monetary value, and the cost-effectiveness of restoration. If an item has significant structural damage, deep charring, or irreversible odor saturation that restoration cannot fully address, replacement might be the more practical option. A professional assessment can help determine if restoration is viable and economically sensible, allowing you to make an informed decision.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider replacement if furniture has severe structural damage, deep charring, or irreversible odor. A professional assessment helps determine if restoration is viable.
